summary: The root طمأن (TmAn) primarily means to be or become quiet, tranquil, or at rest, especially after movement or disturbance.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headword_note: Lane indexes geminate roots with two letters where the Corpus uses three; both spellings are resolved here. Kitab al-Ayn does the same, and also files some weak roots under a different third radical; those are resolved against the Corpus spelling and the al-Ayn headword is kept in the entry.
parts_note: parts[].k: d=Lane's English rendering, a=Arabic, p=apparatus/citation

entries.text: طَمْأَنَ يُطَمْئِنُ طَمْأَنَةً : ـ ـه: سكَّنَه وهدَّأَ من رَوْعه؛ طمأنه أن المريضَ قد حسنت حالُه. ـ ـه: خفضه وحناه؛ طمأنَ ظهره للحِمْل.

classical_note: Arabic-only entries from public-domain classical lexica, ordered by compiler death date. Tier 'root-semantic' (Maqayis) derives all senses of a root from one core idea. Tier 'interpretive' (Mufradat) cites hadith and takes theological positions and is not equivalent evidence. Tier 'earliest-disputed' (Kitab al-Ayn) marks a text whose attribution to al-Khalil ibn Ahmad (d. 786) is contested: the work itself records that his student al-Layth ibn al-Muzaffar completed it after his death, so the 786 date orders the entry but does not assert sole authorship. Kitab al-Ayn is arranged by point of articulation, not alphabetically, and files geminate roots with two letters; the al-Ayn headword actually used is preserved in each entry. Compilation: wizsk/arabic_lexicons, GPL-3.0. Kitab al-Ayn text: OpenITI, ed. Makhzumi and al-Samarra'i (8 vols) — LICENCE NOT CLEARED.
